All industries ↗

Keep client records separate

Accounting firms coordinate recurring checklists, source documents, review notes, deadlines, and client communication across many engagements. Scope each Maia task to one client's channel and approved source set, with links back to the underlying records.

Use separate channels or workspaces, approved source sets, and clear access for each engagement. Accountants remain responsible for checking that the right client's records are in scope and for making the accounting determination.

Prepare the document checklist

Provide the engagement checklist, period, authorized document folder, prior requests, and owner map. Maia can compare expected support with supplied files and list missing, stale, or ambiguous records.

The output can group requests by client contact and internal owner. The engagement manager verifies that each item is actually required and edits the client request before sending it. A filename alone should not count as proof that the document covers the correct period.

Organize close exceptions

Give Maia the current checklist, evidence links, review notes, and due dates. It can produce an exception pulse containing overdue preparation, missing support, unresolved review comments, and blocked dependencies.

Preparers and reviewers decide whether evidence is sufficient and when work is complete. Maia should never close a task, clear a review note, or alter the ledger based on a Slack summary.

Draft approved client reminders

From a verified missing-item list and approved template, Maia can draft a concise request that names the period, record, and due date. It can combine related requests so the client receives one organized message.

The engagement team checks the list and approves the send. Tax positions, accounting conclusions, filing instructions, and advice remain with qualified professionals.

Prepare the engagement handoff

When work moves between preparer, reviewer, or specialist, Maia can summarize completed steps, evidence locations, open questions, client dependencies, and next deadlines. Each statement should point to the engagement record.

The incoming owner confirms the handoff. This keeps review context in the team thread without turning Maia into a practice-management or accounting system.

Start with one client checklist

Choose one engagement with a checklist, document folder, and open review notes. Ask Maia to prepare the missing-item list and draft the client request. The manager can correct the items and wording in Slack, then assign the internal follow-up from the same thread.

The same engagement thread can support a weekly manager review. Maia can bring forward only new missing items, review notes that changed status, and deadlines approaching in the next period. Preparers see where they need help, reviewers see the evidence waiting for attention, and managers can rebalance work without opening every client folder.

Questions from accounting firms

Can Maia prepare tax or accounting advice?

No. Maia organizes records and drafts routine coordination material. Qualified professionals make and communicate all accounting and tax judgments.

How should we keep client work separate?

Assign separate channels, source sets, and access. Review channel membership and connected records for each engagement.

Can Maia send document requests?

It can draft them from a verified checklist. An engagement owner should confirm the items, recipient, and wording before sending.
